clusters.mechanism: Resume always registers legacy worktrees against the bare factory cache (cachePath) and legacy.ts requires a bare owner, so legacy local worktrees attached to the source repository are rejected with 'Unsafe worktree Git administration'.

The migration's eligibility criteria (succeeded prepare or a gate event) exclude a run interrupted after worktree creation but before the first gate event, so its legacy worktree is never marked and registration is skipped.

The migration uses a hard-coded sidecar-introduction timestamp cutoff as a proxy for upgrade time, so legacy worktrees created or prepared after the cutoff (including runs that re-entered prepare) are excluded, and the tests use timestamps just before the cutoff and miss this.
The unconditional headSha git call on resume runs before the needsHumanReason check, so a broken or unrecorded worktree turns a needs_human run into a git/trust failure.
The change greatly exceeds the roughly 20-line budget and duplicates trustedEnv/recordWorktree validation in a separate 71-line module, creating two diverging sources of truth.
